headers.x-deepseek-harness-session-id: The session the request belongs to, stamped when the caller passes options.sessionId. The model gateway reads it to attribute a request's cost to the conversation that made it; a project's catch-all default runs several at once, and the rule it replaced could attribute only when exactly one was running.

modelRequestHeaders.fallback: the project's single active run, as before
modelRequestHeaders.verifiedAgainst: 0.1.7-rc.2, read in the installed closure at @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek@0.1.7-rc.2/lib/index.js (the shared Messages transport the `llm-deepseek` row's `dsh-llm-deepseek-api-key` plugin registers onto)

notes.sessionEventPlumbing: Session records the kernel keeps for its own bookkeeping and the control plane has no use for: the assembled system prompt and request header, route metadata, the title request, the inbox splice, the permission facts written when a session starts, a workspace-change marker, and the three compaction records (`start`, `summary`, `prune`) around the `compaction/end` the control plane decodes as its one `compaction` event. The first nine are recorded verbatim in the 0.1.7-rc.2 golden frames (`apps/server/test/fixtures/dsh/golden-frames.json`); the compaction records are in no recording and are classified by name alone, so their shape is never read. Each name is in `sessionEventTypes`, decodes to `unknown` with its raw type, and is not published to a run's stream; the event pump still follows it for the log's sequence, which is the stall monitor's heartbeat. A type of the kernel's register in neither list is unclassified: counted by raw type for operators, never published. Classifying one is a name in `sessionEventPlumbing` or a RunEvent of its own.
notes.sessionStatusAbsent: There is no session status method. Running state arrives as an `api-session/status` emit on the Gateway-internal `$events` stream.
notes.hostDescribeRemoved: 0.1.2 removed host.describe with the rest of ApiProxy. Host facts arrive once, in the `$events` stream's opening `ready` frame. The readiness probe is session/list, which is a real wire call and therefore also proves authentication.
notes.methodsRenamed: 0.1.2 renamed every method from dotted to slashed and moved arguments into a named descriptor: session.list became session/list taking {_request}. Verified against a running 0.1.2-alpha.3 binary, which 404s the dotted form and names the missing args field itself.
notes.sessionIdNotInFrame: A session's events arrive on the `session/follow` stream opened for that session and no longer carry a session id. Whatever opens the stream owns the pairing.
notes.noVersionField: The wire protocol carries no version field, so method names matching does not prove frame shapes match. Golden frames are the only check that does.
notes.summarizeWithLlmNotExported: dsh-compaction-basic declares summarizeWithLlm in lib/types/summarizer.d.ts, but the published bundle exports only { BasicCompactionEngine, default }: the function is module-internal, and `./src/*` is in `exports` while not being in `files`. src/compaction.mjs therefore reaches the upstream summarization call through the base class's own summarize() hook, which appends its checkpoint-structure directive after ours. If a later release exports it, the EviMed directive can replace the upstream one instead of composing with it.
notes.compactionProviderIsAlsoAComposition: dsh-compaction-basic is a `provider-base`, not a `config-row`, because harness-port subclasses it. It is still named by a composition row and still installed only inside the runtime image, which is why the composition checker treats both roles alike; the distinct word records that a rename of `summarize` silently disables the override rather than erroring.
notes.sessionV4: DSH 0.1.7 uses session format 4. A `tool/result` message is role `tool` with `toolCallId` and `isError` on the message and its content directly in `content` (format 3 wrapped it in one `tool-result` block of a user-role message); a message source names its own producer kind and the bare `plugin` kind is refused, so messages we write carry `plugin:<name>` (`pluginSource`), the kind the kernel's own V3->V4 migration gives our older ones. Format-3 logs on a project volume are read through that migration without being rewritten; the first write open publishes a `session.v4.jsonl.zstd` successor beside the untouched `session.v3.jsonl.zstd`, and a 0.1.5 kernel cannot read a session once it has one. Live assistant deltas still use assistant-stream frames; durable assistant/message contains the completed output and attempt stream. Historical v0 chunks and v3 tool-result wrappers remain readable by the EviMed decoders only.
notes.agentScopedRegistration: Two registrations are made through one agent's own context (`agent.ctx`) at its `agent/created` (0.1.7 folded `agent/session-start` into it), never through the preset's: `tools.restrict` (the root is shown only its own research tools) and `systemPrompt.section` (a delegated child's guidance replaces the orchestration guidance and the answer persona by name). `skills.register` through a child's context is not used: the context does not carry the skills service, and every registration failed on the first live runs (2026-09-19); a child reads a deferred method section from its skill file by line instead. The registries intersect restrictions and let the nearest scope win a section or skill name along a scope chain, and a child joins the preset's standing scope rather than its parent's, so each registration stays with the one agent. A child's session starts inside `ctx.subagents.start` (the kernel creates the agent and awaits its serial `agent/created` listeners before its loop takes queued input), so a registration made there precedes the child's first prompt and first skill catalogue. `agent.steer` wakes an idle agent and is the documented objection at `agent/turn-stopping`; `agent.inject` does neither.
notes.subagentCatalog: There is no `subagents/list` since 0.1.7. A parent's direct children are its own `subagentCatalog` projection, read without activating an agent through `session/projections` (`values.subagentCatalog`: `{ id, createdAt, mode, label? }`, mode `one-shot`, `continuable` or `unknown`), and a child is read at `{ kind: 'subagent', parentSessionId, childSessionId, mode }`, where `unknown` is resolved by the kernel from the child's own descriptor.
notes.presetsAreRows: Presets are host rows since 0.1.7: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets` and its directory roots are gone, a preset is one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row whose `config.plugins` is the agent's entry list, and `agent-preset-registry.config.default` names the one sessions get. The socket ships `evimed-universal` as such a row (`presets/evimed-universal.patch.yml`, generated from the preset directory it edits), and its bundle patch disables the four rows the web bundle declares beside it (`preset-standard`, `preset-ptc`, `preset-minimal`, `preset-cordis`): a session on one of those carries none of our plugins, so `evimed-universal` is the only preset the registry holds and a `session/create` naming another answers `agent-preset/not-found`.

sessionHistory.note: The session's own jump loader (`ISession.loadThrough`, the call `ui-chat`'s turn rail makes). The transcript body reads a finished conversation to its first event with it, because the chat folds a closed turn's process only once `hasMore` is false.

chatNodeHooks.note: Hooks every `conversation.chat.node` occupant receives: the turn's own published values (the closing answer `ui-chat` chose, which its own answer row reads the same way), the chat snapshot (`timeline.turnOrder`), and the kernel's `file` resource (a workspace file's stat, `bytes`). The delivered-files body reads all three.

resultRevisionContext.note: Control-plane-owned reference, staged after the native draft. The official fetch/openStream hooks attach it only to the same session/prompt whose text retains that draft prefix; replacement, navigation, cancellation and disposal clear it. Only an exact same requestId/text retry retains the submitted reference. The control plane reauthorizes the immutable target and removes this envelope before the upstream kernel receives the request. No new upstream service or composer subscription is used.

rightSidebar.note: The kernel's own right column, from `dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right`. Content that belongs beside a conversation registers a tab here; occupying the `rightbar` layout slot would take the whole column instead, which is what the left column already had to be undone from.
